reader.decision: Approve the proposal with the `read_at` guard in `UPSERT_LATEST`. Do not switch to per-device-group consumers. Before merge, confirm that nothing downstream needs `readings` in strict arrival order, and check which errors count as `TransientError`.
reader.decision_reason: The message shows a concrete failure: the retry loop stalls the whole consumer for 62 s, and the 26 October failover backlog peaked at 41,200 messages and took 16 minutes to clear. The one-clause guard closes the stale-overwrite hole that concurrent redelivery opens. The per-device alternative is only needed if `readings` must be in arrival order, and the message does not say that it must.

reconstruction.problem: The hand-written `with_retries` loop in `sparrow-ingest` sleeps 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 s (62 s) on `TransientError`. With `max_ack_pending: 1` the whole consumer waits during that time. `logs/lag-2026-10-26.txt` shows 17 such stalls. On 26 October the failover backlog peaked at 41,200 messages and took 16 minutes to clear.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Replacing the loop with JetStream redelivery and raising `max_ack_pending` to 256 means messages are no longer saved in arrival order. `UPSERT_LATEST` has no `read_at` check and relied on that order. A late redelivery of an old reading, such as R1 at -20 °C at 10:15:07 after R2 at -12 °C had saved, overwrites the newer value in `latest_reading`. That makes the live map wrong and resets the `freezer-temp-high` 10-minute window with a stale value.
reconstruction.fix: Delete `ingest/retry.py`. In `ingest/handler.py`, remove `with_retries`, call `msg.nak(delay=...)` on `TransientError`, and at delivery 6 publish to `ingest.dlq` and ack. In `deploy/consumer.yaml`, change `max_ack_pending` from 1 to 256 and `max_deliver` from 1 to 6. In `ingest/store.py`, add `WHERE latest_reading.read_at < EXCLUDED.read_at` to the `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` in `UPSERT_LATEST`. The stale reading still gets its `readings` history row.
reconstruction.cost: The guard is one SQL clause and costs nothing at normal load. The `readings` table may now receive rows out of arrival order. The message could not check which errors are `TransientError`, because `ingest/errors.py` and `ingest/parse.py` were not found. The per-device-group alternative would cost more consumers to deploy and tune.

follow_up_questions: Does any consumer of `readings` need rows written in strict arrival order? If yes, the per-device-group consumers become the primary option.
Which errors count as `TransientError`? `ingest/errors.py` and `ingest/parse.py` were not found, so this is unchecked. It decides which failures get redelivered and which go to `ingest.dlq`.
reader.closing_answer: I approve the proposal with the `read_at` guard in `UPSERT_LATEST`, not the per-device-group consumers. The approval is conditional on confirming that `readings` does not need strict arrival order, and on checking the `TransientError` classification before merge.
